## 318375: exact fixed-composition reduction, not an entropy shortcut

Original0903.4554 complete three-page text read. It uses GF(2) upper bidiagonal R: y_i=x_i xor x_(i+1) for i<n, y_n=x_n. Source Figure1 caption/text specify n30204/61408, fixed numbers of ones, random placement, ten samples; no program or experiment was run here. Empirical entropy metric n h2(w/n) is distinct from joint Shannon entropy H(X). Invertibility gives H(RX)=H(X), but does not identify the expected plug-in entropy of one realization. Thus invoking Shannon alone fails.

For a binary input with h ones and z=n-h zeros, 0<h<n, let r be its number of maximal one-runs. Then w=2r when x starts0, w=2r-1 when x starts1: each one-run contributes an entering and exiting transition, except initial run has no entering transition; last-bit term pays the otherwise absent terminal exit. Positive one-run lengths have binom(h-1,r-1) compositions. For starts0, distribute z zeros into r positive preceding/interior slots and one nonnegative terminal slot: binom(z,r). For starts1, r-1 positive interior zero slots and a nonnegative terminal slot give binom(z,r-1). Hence exact expected output empirical entropy is
n/binom(n,h) sum_(r>=1) binom(h-1,r-1)[binom(z,r) h2(2r/n)+binom(z,r-1) h2((2r-1)/n)],
with impossible binomials interpreted0. This is an all-parameter symbolic combinatorial derivation, no finite enumeration/numerical evaluation. Constant inputs handled separately: h0 maps to weight0; hn maps to weight1. It is not legitimate to treat those as high-entropy evidence.

Second route: uniform fixed-composition input has joint entropy log2 binom(n,h), and output has same entropy. Conditioning on output weight W gives H(Y)=H(W)+H(Y|W)<=H(W)+E log2 binom(n,W). This yields a lower bound on expected combinatorial log binomial length, but the H(W) penalty is not bounded by1 in general and log binomial differs from n h2. It does not prove desired strict inequality. Third route: Jensen supplies E h2(W/n)<=h2(EW/n), the WRONG direction for bounding saving from above. Exact unpaid target is the above finite sum > n h2(h/n)-1 over an explicitly stated intended range, plus source clarification of range and average. No small endpoint is credited.
